correctness.rationale: All 15 positive differences in each six-point set are {1,...,13,16,17}, each once. The signed measure autocorrelations therefore match. Exact convolution with the common block progression gives matching center autocorrelations for every m; disjoint disk indicators give identical full continuous planar covariograms. The sorted consecutive gaps are (1,3,6,2,5) versus (1,7,3,2,4), with interblock gap 5. At enlarged disk radius strictly between 3 and 7/2, exactly m B-type gaps exceed contact distance; no A-type gaps do. The explicit checker executed and passed 61 finite m configurations; universal proof is algebraic, not empirical.

originality.rationale: The signed-homometric six-point pair and convolution method are fully credited to older work. The claimed addition is the explicit unbounded, linear-in-disk-count connected-component discrepancy of Euclidean offsets of *positive-area smooth-component planar sets sharing the entire continuous covariogram*, stable over a nonzero interval of radii. Available source checks and prior statement comparisons do not imply this precise topological statement. Full historic priority remains uncertain.

No uniqueness or optimal 1/6 constant is proved; only sharp linear growth order is asserted.
Other nonindexed geometric tomography/topological morphology sources might already state an equivalent counterfamily.

value.rationale: The full vector-displacement law and Fourier intensity encode every two-point translation correlation, a canonical observable of planar shape. For 6m smooth equal disks the exact same observable coexists with 1 versus m+1 connected offset components at a fixed, robust scale. This proves an order-optimal obstruction (linear in m) to detecting a natural topological feature from two-point data; it is stronger than an isolated noncongruent homometric pair and matters for limits of second-order geometric tomography.
